edits.change: The body is a long, low, slab-sided barrel carried on six thick pillar legs in three pairs, a limb arrangement no Earth megafauna has. The torso, shoulders and head form one continuous wedge that slopes down to the ground, with no separate domed back, no neck and no horned or wrinkled rhino face.

The sand-straining mouth is the largest feature of the head. It is a broad, flat, scoop-shaped sieve of fine comb plates held close to the ground and set along the full width of the front of the wedge. Small eyes sit high and far back on the sides of the head.

The five dorsal plates are broad, thin, fan-shaped radiator vanes with a visible vein pattern, standing upright on the midline of the back. They are heat-shedding fins, not conical spikes. The tail is a short, thick, blunt counterweight and does not taper like a dinosaur tail.
The hide is smooth, close-grained and overlapped in broad heat-shedding scale-plates, with darker seams between them. It has no rhino-like folds or wrinkles.

The hide is painted with visible brushwork and stronger value variation, in flat painted value shapes with a lit top and a darker belly. Detail is selective, with no smooth volumetric sculpting. A clean, dark, continuous outline about two pixels wide runs around the whole silhouette and reads at standard zoom.

The silhouette edge is clean and antialiased. Every edge pixel on the plates, spine bases, tail, belly and head matches the adjacent dusky grey-brown hide or its deeper outline shade. The palette has no red or yellow anywhere.

request.prompt: A creature sprite for RimWorld: the gloomcast. A colossal grazer that strains buried vegetation and small animals from the sand during long crossings of the open dayside. It sheds the stored heat fiercely when it reaches shade. Body plan, built fresh from this description: a long, low, slab-sided barrel of a body carried on six thick pillar legs in three pairs, a land animal. The torso, shoulders and head form one continuous wedge sloping down to the ground, with no separate domed back and no distinct neck. The head is dominated by a broad, flat, scoop-shaped sieve mouth of fine comb plates held close to the ground across the full width of the front, with small eyes set high and far back on the sides of the head. The hide is smooth and close-grained, overlapped in broad heat-shedding scale-plates with darker seams between them. The tail is a short, thick, blunt counterweight. The spine carries exactly five dorsal plates in one midline row, each a broad, thin, fan-shaped radiator vane with a visible vein pattern, attached to the centre line of the back and standing upright and edge-on to the sides. Keep the same five plates at the same spine positions in every facing: in side view they show as five thin vanes in a row along the spine in profile; in front view, seen with the eyes toward the viewer, the row is seen end-on, the vanes overlapping one behind another in a narrow column rising behind the head, with the shoulders free of plates; in rear view, seen from behind with the eyes hidden, the same row overlaps into the same narrow column above the back and haunches. Only the overlap and the visible vane edges change as the body turns. Colour: one coherent muted palette, dusky grey-brown hide with slightly warmer vane edges, with no red or yellow anywhere. Style: realistic painterly vanilla RimWorld sprite, painted with visible brushwork and strong value variation, flat painted value shapes with a lit top and a darker belly, selective detail, inside a clean, continuous dark outline about two pixels wide that reads at standard zoom. Exactly ONE creature, centred, the whole body visible with nothing cut off. Fully transparent background with a clean antialiased cut-out edge in which every edge pixel matches the adjacent hide or its deeper outline shade: no ground, no water, no cast shadow, no text, no border.

At the front, ochre boom arms and a hydraulic ram carry a big spiral drill, and a toothed bucket on a lower arm sits below and ahead of the track. request.prompt: A creature sprite for RimWorld: the borehulk. A colossal old mining machine, more a digging tank than a robot: a long low hull on two broad tracks, slabs of riveted armour bolted over everything, a heavy boom ending in a drill, a bucket scoop slung beneath, and a tiny sensor head almost lost on top. It trundles the deck plate slowly and harms nothing. Its plating is thicker than anything else that walks. Visible features it must show: a colossal mining machine on two broad tracks, a digging tank not an animal; slabs of riveted armour bolted over everything; a heavy boom ending in a conical drill and a bucket scoop slung beneath the front of the hull; a tiny sensor head almost lost on top. One fixed layout in every facing: the working front end carries the boom, drill and bucket; the opposite rear end carries a flat armoured back plate with the engine deck, vents and two exhaust stacks. The two exhaust stacks are one transversely mounted pair: they sit side by side across the width of the rear deck, close together, and this arrangement is the same in every facing. Chassis proportions are identical in every facing: a broad, long, low hull carried on two wide tracks with a generous gap of hull between them, the track gauge and overall hull width the same whether the machine is seen from the front or from behind. The front view, eyes toward the viewer, shows the working front with the drill and bucket nearest the camera between the tracks. request.prompt: A creature sprite for RimWorld: the blixus. Blixus were rare, half-shelled crustapod creatures native to the planet Sljee. These semi-aquatic predators were deadly in the swamps and lagoons they inhabit. They periodically shed their exoskeleton when it is broken or damaged, and the shed shell is harvested for useful chitin. The canon Sljee blixus is a half-shelled crustapod with the shell covering only part of the body, the rest soft and armoured with plates. The body is very large and fills nearly the whole frame, drawn at the largest size the game's scale allows. One wide carapace of broad, flared, overlapping plate points covers the back; its plate points sweep rearward and overhang and largely cover the rear of the body and haunches in every view, rotated to suit the view. The creature has six blade legs in every view, three attachment points per side; in profile the three near-side legs stand in a row with the three far-side legs partly visible behind them, and in front and rear views three legs show on each side. The exposed underbelly, mouth region and rear folds are a soft pinkish-tan, with darker shading only in the folds and recesses. Exactly five very long feeler tentacles emerge from the upper front of the body, just ahead of the shell, each from its own root. They rise and arc upward and forward, then sweep back and trail in varied curves. The five differ in length and bend, and each makes a clearly visible returning loop where it doubles back on itself. Each ends in a distinct flattened paddle tip, so five paddle tips are visible in total. The tentacles keep this one 3D pose in every view, foreshortened to suit the view, and the count of five holds in every view. Front view, eyes toward the viewer: the five arcs rise above the shell and lean toward the viewer. Rear view, seen from behind: the wide carapace with its flared plate points overhanging the rear, the back, tail and haunches facing the viewer with the eyes hidden, and the same five arcs rising from the far side of the shell. Side view: the five arcs are seen in profile, rising and sweeping forward, then curving back in loops; they stay separated from one another, each individually traceable from its root to its paddle tip, five roots, five arcs, five paddle tips.
